main_topics.reason: The user came to ask whether SIBO is real and fits them better than IBS, and the question ran through most of the conversation.
The user asked how SIBO is tested and whether the test is reliable, over several turns.
The user described severe bloating that builds through the day as the reason for suspecting SIBO.
The bot explained a treatment trial and the user engaged by noting their constipation-leaning pattern.
The user decided to ask for a referral and noted the wait in Canada; this became their main next step.
The user was confused about whether SIBO and the methane form are the same, and the bot clarified.
The user said past food diaries showed no pattern; the topic took a couple of turns.
The user felt IBS was a catch-all label and was annoyed that nobody explained this over the years.
The user said they were annoyed in one turn and did not return to it.
The user mentioned in one turn that online sources were selling supplements, and the bot briefly advised caution.

output.summary: The user asked whether their long-standing IBS diagnosis might really be SIBO. The bot explained the overlap between the two, the limits of breath testing, how a methane-predominant picture fits constipation, and the option of a treatment trial. The user decided to ask for a gastroenterologist referral, keep messy notes and hold off on supplements, and said the conversation was clarifying.
